imageAlt: A suspicious email marked with a security warning
title: Treat unexpected links as unverified
summary: A familiar logo or urgent message cannot prove who sent it. Verify requests through a trusted route before signing in, paying, or opening an attachment.
body: Phishing messages try to persuade people to reveal information, open a harmful attachment or visit a fraudulent website. They may imitate a known company, colleague or service, and they often create urgency to discourage careful checking.

Do not use the message's link or phone number to verify a surprising request. Instead, open the service's official app, type a known website address yourself, or contact the person using a number you already trust. Check the actual sender and destination, but remember that names and logos can be copied.

If a message looks suspicious, use the reporting feature in your email or workplace tools. If you already entered a password, change it through the official service and review its account-security options. For work accounts or devices, report the event promptly using your organisation's process.
takeaways: Verify unusual requests through a separate, trusted channel.
Avoid signing in from unexpected message links.
Report suspicious messages and act quickly if you shared credentials.
